body:
## Observation

`tests/unit/test_1094_failed_conversion_imports_original.py::TestConversionDeadline::test_convert_book_passes_the_deadline_to_the_converter`
failed once during a full `pytest -m "smoke or unit" -n auto` run on
`feat/reader-notes` (2026-08-10), in a run whose only other change was six `.po`
files and one test file — nothing touching conversion, deadlines or subprocess.

Three controls, all pointing the same way:

- passes **in isolation** on that branch
- passes **in isolation** on `main`
- **absent** from the same branch's own pre-fix full run 20 minutes earlier,
  which failed 5 other tests and not this one

So it is order- or concurrency-dependent under xdist, not a defect in the change
that surfaced it.

## Why it is worth a finding rather than a shrug

A test that fails once per N full runs and passes on retry is the most expensive
kind: it trains everyone to re-run rather than read, which is precisely the habit
that lets a genuine red through. That is not hypothetical here — this session
watched three real failures sit inside a wall of billing corpses, where the
"re-run it" reflex would have laundered them.

It also lands on a specific seam: `--maxfail=3` in the Fast Tests lane truncates
the FAILED list to a prefix, so a flake occupying one of those three slots can
hide a real failure behind it.

## Where to look

Deadline assertions are time-sensitive by construction, and under `-n auto` a
worker can be descheduled long enough to blow a wall-clock margin — the usual
shape is an assertion on elapsed/remaining time rather than on the value passed.
`--dist=loadfile` already pins a file to one worker, so cross-file interference
is the less likely half; shared module state or a monkeypatched clock leaking
between tests in the same file is the more likely.

Reproduce with repeated full runs rather than targeted ones — a targeted run is
exactly the condition under which it passes.
title: test_1094 TestConversionDeadline fails only under -n auto, and passes in isolation on both the branch and main
